With so much to look forward to and wager on, college football betting enthusiasts have a lot to take in every season.

Our college football guide has you covered on how to approach betting on the 2026 FBS season, how to bet on college football at sports betting sites such as Lucky Rebel and BetOnline, and strategies, tips, and resources for college football handicapping and betting.

Both new and experienced bettors can benefit from this guide. Let’s dive into what you can find here.

Explore Our College Football Guides to Hone Your Handicapping Skills

College football betting involves much more than picking winners each week. From researching matchups and evaluating betting lines to deciding when to place your bets or how to approach live betting, there is a lot for bettors to consider. Our college football betting guides can help you navigate those different parts of the process.

Whether you are preparing for the upcoming weekend or evaluating season-long betting opportunities, our guides cover a variety of topics to help you make more informed decisions. Our weekly college football betting checklist provides a seven-day routine for researching matchups, tracking odds and news, and preparing your bets.

Our guides also cover some of the biggest betting events of the college football season. Learn how to approach Heisman Trophy betting, explore College Football Playoff betting opportunities, and find out what to consider when wagering on games and futures during the postseason.

From weekly handicapping and betting strategies to season-long futures and the postseason, these resources can help you prepare for the different betting opportunities that arise throughout the college football season.

2026 Heisman Trophy Odds and Contenders

The Heisman Trophy race is one of the biggest season-long betting markets in college football, and the outlook can change considerably from week to week. Individual performances, team success, injuries, and the results of major matchups can all influence Heisman Trophy odds as the season progresses.

Here is a look at some of the leading contenders and their current Heisman Trophy odds:

Odds are from Bovada as of Sunday, October 25, 2026.

Player Position Team Odds
Jeremiah Smith WR Ohio State +115
Darian Mensah QB Miami (FL) +325
Malachi Toney WR Miami (FL) +350
CJ Carr QB Notre Dame +2000

Trinidad Chambliss QB Ole Miss +2800

Gio Lopez QB Wake Forest +6500
Sam Leavitt QB LSU +8000

Although quarterbacks have dominated the award in recent years, Smith is on course to buck that trend in 2026.

We will update this section with the latest odds and developments involving the leading Heisman Trophy contenders. For a closer look at the award, its history, and the factors to consider when evaluating the betting market, visit our Heisman Trophy betting guide.

Biggest Games, Rivalry Matchups, and Upsets of the 2026 Season

From early-season showdowns between national championship contenders to historic rivalry games and postseason matchups, the 2026 college football schedule is packed with games worth following.

Some of these matchups will have major implications on the college football standings and the College Football Playoff race. Others carry decades of history and bragging rights that extend well beyond the standings. Our guide to the biggest college football rivalries explores what makes these matchups unique and the factors bettors should consider when evaluating them.

Below, we highlight some of the biggest games and rivalry matchups of the 2026 season, along with their scheduled dates and results. We will update the tables as games are completed and add postseason matchups as they become available.

Note: Results in which an unranked or lower-ranked team defeated a higher-ranked team are in bold.

September 2026

September features several major nonconference matchups, the renewal of longstanding rivalries, and the beginning of conference play.

Conference play will also bring some important early tests for national championship contenders, including LSU’s trip to Ole Miss and several notable SEC and Big Ten matchups to close out the month.

November 2026

November is one of the most important months of the college football season. Conference championship races enter their final stages, the College Football Playoff selection committee begins releasing its rankings, and teams compete to strengthen their postseason credentials.

The month also features several of the sport’s most anticipated annual rivalries. From the Holy War to the Iron Bowl, Egg Bowl, and The Game, intense rivalry clashes will provide a fitting conclusion to the regular season.

With conference championship appearances and College Football Playoff berths potentially on the line, the results of these matchups could have significant consequences for the postseason picture.

December 2026

December marks the transition from the regular season to the postseason. Conference championship games will determine several automatic College Football Playoff berths, while the annual Army-Navy Game provides one final regular-season rivalry matchup before bowl season gets underway.

The College Football Playoff begins on December 18, with four first-round games taking place over two days. The Fiesta Bowl will then host the first quarterfinal on December 30, with the remaining quarterfinals scheduled for New Year’s Day.

We will update the December table with participating teams and results as conference championship matchups, bowl games, and the College Football Playoff bracket are finalized.

January 2027

The college football season reaches its conclusion in January, beginning with three College Football Playoff quarterfinals on New Year’s Day. The Cotton Bowl, Peach Bowl, and Rose Bowl will determine the final three semifinalists, joining the winner of December’s Fiesta Bowl.

The Orange Bowl and Sugar Bowl will host the semifinals on January 14 and 15, respectively, before the final two teams meet at Allegiant Stadium in Las Vegas on January 25 to determine the national champion.
